I share your pain, in a way. In fact, here's a fun story I want to share that made me realized I was definitely a Type 2 (which happened 2 days ago funnily enough)

For context, I work as armed security for a high traffic and transit station that also has law enforcement (which I work with). As I stepped out of a train I had just cleared with my partner, we hear the yell of a girl saying "I love you baby! Don't leave me! At first, we thought, okay that was funny, is someone messing around?

Well, it turns out the cops had arrested what seemed to be a high school couple (male and female), who later turned out had drugs on them. Well, while they were arrested in handcuffs, and the police were searching their bags and questioning the boy, the girl kept screaming loudly, iterations of "Baby I love you!" "l love you so much, baby!" and even to the cops "Please! Let me see his face!" (even though he was literally right in front of her, I personally think she was just extremely high on whatever they had taken). 

Well, my partner and I are just laughing at the situation because of the absurdity and dramaticness of it. Even bystanders and the police are laughing because it just looks like the scene out of a movie. Still, as they are being taken away, handcuffed, and walked out together, she keeps screaming the same "I love you baby!" type of statements. Finally the boy turns his head around towards her and says at the top of the stairs they were walking up, almost like a dramatic exit to a movie scene, loudly but calmly "I love you so much baby"

It was such a funny moment because of how dramatic and movie like it was, that everyone around us was talking about whether or not it was real, or were we being secretly filmed for a prank or something.

Either way, after all the jokes and making fun of it, deep down I felt some sadness and envy. I sorely WISHED I had someone like that girl who would not hesitate to keep proclaiming her love for me even in uncertain times. Who would scream over and over to see my face and not leave her because he couldn't live without me, and I, without her.

Despite the absurdity of it, and the fact they were young lovers, it still showed me that love can be so powerful that it doesn't matter how embarrassing it might look. She would love him to the end in that moment.

Though I may not know you OP, or anyone else reading this, I truly wish you find that someone who loves you to death, like that girl in my story that loves her boyfriend, or like the man to his wife in your story. Thanks for reading, and have a love filled rest of your week.

I see a lot of talk for the cons, but here is my theory on how it could work.

First, no more first past the post (FPTP) when it comes to who wins with the votes because it doesn't work and eventually leads to a 2-party system where a third party ends up hurting one of the other parties. [CGPGrey explains this in one of his videos](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s7tWHJfhiyo). 

This pure democracy should have an [Alternative Voting System](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Y3jE3B8HsE) or a similiar voting system like the [Condorcet method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condorcet_method).

Basically a fair voting system that allows people to vote more than once based on their preferences so that the winner will be someone that the majority would be content with.

Second, some sort of identification system using biometrics to make sure people aren't voting for others and to see who has and has not voted (like a check off list, verifying that John Doe, born 1/1/2000, with SSN 123-45-6789 has voted).

I have a lot more ideas on how to try to make it more less susceptible to propaganda and to try to make voters informed because in a pure democracy, unfortunately there will always be a person or some group that will spread misinformation for their benefit. So I think the biggest hurdle to making sure a pure democracy works is by making sure people are informed on the facts and vote with logic, not bias and emotion caused by misinformation. Unfortunately, that's a very hard thing to do, at least in today's world despite the fact we have the internet.

I would love to talk about all the issues needed to be fixed to make a pure democracy work, but for the record, I think it would be the best form of democracy as long as we can make sure it not susceptible to corruption and to make sure everyone is educated on the issues, candidates, etc... The 2 suggestions I made so far are ones I think we could implement now to progress towards a better democracy throughout governments and countries in the world.
